learning_outcomes.text: Provide the basic elements of the language of technical communication in industry, in order to put the student able to correctly perform and interpret technical drawings.
Describe the organs of machines and their modes of representation.
To provide the basics of computer aided design.

Systematic knowledge and understanding of the key aspects of mechanical design of industrial engineering and its methods. In particular: understanding of which are the most suitable methods in order to define a product and its characteristics; technologies for their production and their graphic representation.
Knowledge of the most suitable production process for the production of mechanical components and for the representation of drawing dimensions, geometric and dimensional tolerances.

The ability to choose and apply appropriate analytical, modelling, verification and experimental methods for the interpretation and production of drawings of parts and assemblies; the basic sizing and functional verification of components and mechanical groups.

The ability to choose the most suitable production process for the production of mechanical components for their correct representation with particular reference to issues related to the definition of geometric and dimensional tolerances.
Written technical communication (reports, deliverables).
Graphic representation and communication (drafting of diagrams, graphs and tables).
Understanding of technical standards.
To respect commitments and deadlines.
Ability to analyse data and information using established methods and tools, interpret results, and draw consistent conclusions, also with the support of provided guidelines.
Ability to compare different engineering solutions and contribute to technically justified decisions by referring to engineering standards and established industrial procedures.
Ability to work effectively in teams, understanding the engineering context of a problem and recognizing the main interdisciplinary implications of the application domain.

Ability to organize one's work while meeting assigned deadlines, managing available time and resources effectively, realistically assessing one's own capabilities, and contributing to task prioritization.
Ability to recognize personal knowledge limitations and the need for further learning, identifying appropriate information sources and guided learning opportunities.

Ability to communicate and convey information, ideas, problems, and solutions in engineering contexts to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, using appropriate technical language and referring to familiar application scenarios.
Ability to present engineering problems, solutions, analyses, and results clearly and systematically through written reports and oral presentations, following standard formats and conventions.

Ability to graphically represent and communicate technical data, results, and solutions through the preparation of technical drawings, diagrams, graphs, and tables using established standards and conventions.
Ability to independently, although primarily under guidance, acquire and update knowledge in the relevant engineering field using established educational resources and learning tools.

Ability to identify and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation through the main available resources (libraries, databases, technical manuals, and digital sources), selecting relevant information with appropriate guidance.

Ability to learn through project-based and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) methodologies by applying acquired knowledge and engineering tools to case studies and real-world problems of appropriate complexity.

syllabus_topics: Sections with surfaces of any shape
System shaft base and hole base
Chains and series of shares tolerated
Indication of the geometric tolerances in drawings
Indication of roughness in the drawings
Bodies for the transmission of motion

assessment_methods.method: Written test: drawing of a standard mechanical component (bearing, toothed wheel, threaded connection)
Written test: one or more exercises on dimensional and/or geometrical tolerances
Written test: Shot peening of a mechanical assembly
Written test: drawing of one or more parts of the assembly

assessment_rules: The overall assessment includes a written test. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) for serious conceptual errors to 29-30 and Honors (Lode) for excellent, in-depth knowledge and independent operation. Honors is awarded for work distinguished by brilliance and originality.
